Tom / Aisha — technical follow-up. A few clarifications from the infra side: 

1) Connectivity patterns we support
- VPC peering: we can accept peering connections from customer VPCs into a Redwood-managed VPC where inference endpoints live. Peering is L3; no transitive routing is enabled from our side. We can confirm route tables we require and will provide explicit route prefixes.
- Private endpoints (PrivateLink-style): supported in AWS via interface endpoints. These are preferred for customers who cannot accept peering. Endpoint DNS is regional; we can provide the CNAME/DNS labels to map to endpoint interfaces.

2) Egress IP behavior
- For hosted endpoints, outbound requests to external services originate from our egress NAT pool. Listed egress ranges are provided in the attached ZIP. For private deployments where traffic stays within a VPC, outbound egress is customer-controlled unless you route through Redwood-managed NATs (optional).

3) IP allowlist vs CIDR granularity
- We provide a set of /24 CIDRs for allowlisting. If you require single IPs, we can document per-region NAT IPs (note these are subject to change on a quarterly schedule; we publish a stable manifest with 30 days notice).

4) Route propagation and leakage
- We do not enable BGP route propagation into customer route tables from our side. For peering, only explicit routes you add will be visible in your VPC. For PrivateLink there is no route table modification required on the customer VPC.

I've attached a quick diagram (sig-network-diagram.png) that shows both flow patterns. Also noted an optional fallback: if peering is not permitted, we can set up a dedicated reverse-proxy in your VPC (customer-managed) that talks to Redwood over the interface endpoint.

If you can confirm which connectivity model Clinica prefers, we'll finalize the annotated SIG answers and the allowlist evidence bundle.

— Soojin
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — helpful. A couple of questions after reviewing the draft: 

- Can you confirm the specific /24 CIDRs per region you expect us to allow? The security team prefers CIDRs over single IPs.
- For VPC peering, will you provide a sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet we can validate? We need to ensure peering connection reset behavior and that your side won’t inject additional routes.
- Is there any TLS termination on your edge where we should provide SAN entries for cert validation?

Also, please provide any audit/log evidence that shows an example connection (pcap not necessary) and a short note on how you retain flow logs for 90 days (SOC requirement). We saw the TODOs in the PDF.

Best,
Emma Lane
Security Engineer, Clinica Health

- Peering snippet: included (terraform/peering-sample.tf) — it shows the peering resource and explicit route table entries (no route propagation enabled).

- Audit/logs: included a 7-day scrubbed flow log sample in the ZIP and a short note on our retention (90 days by default for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private deployments can request longer retention via the contract addendum).

Next steps: please confirm which connectivity model Clinica will use and we will produce a final signed evidence bundle for your records. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you’d like to walk the artifacts.
